page.layout: One block of text in a single column, with two circular portrait medallions above it. The medallions are illustrations with inscriptions around their rims, read first, left then right. Running head at top, page number at top right. No margin notes or footnotes.

main_text.p: DANIEL Propheta vaticinabatur tempore Iechoniæ, & Ieremiæ. Hic à Nabuchodonofore cum sodalibus captiuus ab-ductus est, anno mundi 3348. ante Christum natum 614. Chal-dæorum artes & linguam 3. an. didicit: Somnia Regis Nabucho donosor expofuit, & vifionem Baltafaris. in lacum leonum coniectus, atque inde eductus est: Sufannam liberauit. De somnio 4. beftiarum quæ 4. mundi regna fignabant: vtque ei 70. hebdo. visionem edifferuerit Gabriel Angelus, & pleraque alia qui cupit nosse, legat huius Danielis librum, & Iofeph. lib. 10. cap. 12. Hic instabat assiduis precibus apud Deū, pro Nabuchodono-fore transformato, prædixitque vt formam & regnum recupe-raret: quare indidit ei rex Nabuch. nomen Baltasaris filij sui: voluitque eum filiis cohæredem instituere, quod ille recusauit. Vide Epiphan.Obiit Daniel in Babylone, & sepultus est in spe-lunca regali, honorificè.

EZECHIEL Propheta tempore Ieremiæ, Baruch, & Danielis Prophetarum, extitit: hic adhuc puer cum aliis in Babyloniam captiuus ab-ductus est, vbi prophetare incepit anno mundi 3349. ante Christum natum 613. anno tamen ætatis suæ 30. ait Ieron. in Chaldæa prophetasse Ezechielem: tum cùm Ieremias in Iudæa. eius vide Prophetiam, & Iosef. lib. Antiqui. 10. cap. 9. Et Ecclesiaft. ca. 49. In Babylone iudicauit tribum Dan & Gad: prædixitque culpa earum, non reuersurum populum Hierosolymam, quoad resipiscerent: quare exacerbati diftraxerunt eum equis per crepidines saxorum, & excerebrarūt eum, & sepelierunt in sepulchro Sem & Arphaxad. Vide chro. Guill.

page.notes: Two woodcut portrait medallions above the text: left, a bearded/long-haired figure labelled PROPH. DANIEL; right, a figure labelled PROPH. EZECHIEL. Their inscriptions are transcribed above. Reading of "Iofeph." and "excerebrarūt" is from a slightly soft scan; the "Ezechiel" text, Baruch and Chaldaea passages are legible. No other doubtful readings.
